title: Weaver's Wharf
story:
As The Waterlily cleared the deep, echoing shadow of Scholar's Arch, the central district of Oakhaven exploded into morning light and motion. James had never heard so many human voices talking all at once. James had never smelled so many rich spices mixing with roasted nuts and coal smoke. James had never seen buildings tall enough to steal the sky, their painted wooden balconies overlapping like the high terraces of the Great Canopy.

Silas worked the long wooden tiller with practiced ease, guiding the heavy barge away from the main canal traffic and toward a bustling wooden quay known as Weaver's Wharf. Along the stone embankments, merchants shouted prices over crates of bright citrus, rolls of woven cloth, and gleaming tin kettles. Silas cast a thick hemp rope around a iron mooring cleat with a soft, heavy thud. He turned to James, offered a slow nod of farewell, and pointed toward the wooden stairs leading up into the market square.

James touched the brass map canister hanging at his side, feeling the steady weight of Barnaby's drawn lines beneath the metal. He raised his green sea-glass to his eye for just a moment, watching the chaotic, bustling crowd transform into a calm emerald sea. 

Stepping off the deck of the barge, James leaped lightly onto the flat head of a tall wooden mooring post at the edge of the wharf. High above the swirling tide of human boots and trailing coats, he took a deep breath of the city's crisp air. Across the square, a long blue banner fluttered lazily against a high clock tower, beckoning him further into the heart of Oakhaven.
